prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Offshore wind O&M; scope: offshore assets, marine/shore facilities, personnel, external orgs, electrical up to Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere: farm/transmission boundary, dispatch, authorized signals, supply/protection status); excludes public grid, non-farm port ops. Turbine Controller (Glassfin): executes authorized control, limits output, blocks protection-conflicting commands, reports state, safe mode on auxiliary loss; produces Pitch Deviation Notice. Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet (interlocks), Nacelle Condition Monitor. Turbine Sensor Bus collects measurements from Turbine Controller, Pitch System, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor. Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur): imagery. Offshore Substation (Morrowick): Main Transformer, export cable, Export Cable Monitor, station service transformers; sends Transformer Tap Snapshot on review request; consulted on electrical-impact events; Substation Operator confirms constraints. Emergency Generator (Foxglove): auto-starts on auxiliary loss, V/f limits, no unapproved paralleling/export, sheds nonessential, failure→alarm keeping UPS. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale): time-stamped observations/alarms to Shore Control Room (Amber Quay); keeps source/timestamp/turbine ID; flags work from Pitch Deviation Notice; produces Session Revocation Receipt. Shore Control Room escalates alerts over threshold/developing hazard. Control Engineer: validates (range, freshness, timestamp, consistency), uses trends, cross-checks Turbine Controller/Nacelle Condition Monitor; stale/implausible→unverified, not sole basis for intrusive task; records accept/reject/monitor basis; follows approved procedure, confirms state; requests on-site inspection. Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown): receives validated condition info; ranks work using Squall Window Bulletin; produces Deferred Task Rationale (not safety claim). Duty Planner: reviews queue and accepted alerts, selects mobilization (CTV/Daughter Craft/SOV/Helideck), checks parts/competence/limits; adjusts plan on delay/cancellation/access change; Transfer Manifest Addendum→Vessel Master before departure. Priority: safety/major generation loss>routine; personnel risk restricts work. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard): allocation, vessel/crew; uses Position Quality Flag. Grid Dispatcher: dispatch, frequency response; alarms safety>protection>export. Field Supervisor validates faults. Marine Coordinator: daily plan, route reassessment, updated forecast before departure. Vessel Master: accepts/pauses/aborts approach. Crew

Document units:
S311: Inspection findings are compared with the original observations before the alert is closed or converted into corrective work.
S312: The Crew Transfer Vessel uses the Harness Audit Card to verify the applicable equipment checks before personnel transfer.
S313: The Blade Inspection Drone produces the Leading Edge Tile Image during a close-range survey of the blade surface.
S314: Larkspur shall repeat a close-range pass when image coverage is insufficient to assess the suspected surface condition.
S315: The Blade Specialist reviews available inspection evidence and reports whether further examination is warranted.
S316: The Control Engineer reassesses the alert after field findings or corrected sensor data become available.
S317: The Shore Control Room retains the decision record, supporting observations, and response outcome for operational review.
S318: Permit controls coordinate approved work scope, electrical isolation, field execution, and return to service without treating authorization as proof of a safe electrical state.
S319: The Duty Planner submits a defined task scope, work location, crew, and requested operating window for review.
S320: The Field Supervisor confirms that the proposed method, access arrangements, and work party are suitable for the task.
S321: Redoubt shall block permit release until required risk reviews and isolation references are complete.
S322: The HSE Officer reviews task hazards and confirms that required controls are assigned before the permit is authorized.
S323: The Weather Analyst uses the Wave Burst Record to assess whether the planned access period remains suitable.
S324: The Port Agent issues the Berth Slot Confirmation for the planned work period.
S325: The Electrical Technician identifies the electrical sources, isolation points, and verification steps required by the approved scope.
S326: The Substation Operator applies authorized switching actions and records the resulting equipment state.
S327: For turbine work, the Electrical Technician verifies the relevant local isolation and secures the equipment against unintended energization.
S328: Turbine Lockout is maintained while personnel are exposed to the identified hazards.
S329: Work begins only after the Field Supervisor confirms that the permit is active and the required isolations have been independently verified.
S330: The Field Supervisor briefs the crew on the permit limits, isolation boundaries, communications, and conditions requiring work to stop.
S331: The Electrical Technician proves the test instrument, tests for absence of voltage, and proves the instrument again where the procedure requires it.
S332: The Personnel Tracking Console supports confirmation that personnel assigned to the task are accounted for at the work location.
